page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved top-tier ratings in memory bandwidth, with read-only large block speeds of 436.06 GB/sec and write large block speeds of 184.19 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and memory scores also reached top-tier classifications. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 66283.59 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19664.0. However, single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1661.0. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the bottom 10% at 4.66 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E32ps_v6 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads due to its dedicated ARM cores and high-capacity memory architecture. The absence of bundled local storage allows users to scale external storage independently, avoiding costs for unused local capacity. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing. It is less suitable for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance or large-scale LLM inference.
